info.title: Slatebox API
info.description: Use a personal access token from Profile → Developer access. Every route is generated from the action registry; the same actions back the app. Calls made with a token report their rate limit in RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset.

get.description: The AI connections you, your team and this server have (never their keys), which one each feature uses (chat, generation, presentation, vision, images, shape, and the default), and which connection serves each feature for you now (effective), with what it cannot do. ownProviders false means this server uses only the AI its operator set up.

200.description: Done.

put.description: Your own or your team's AI: adds or changes connections (a cloud provider with its key, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with its address, optional key and model), removes some, and chooses which connection each feature uses. level me changes yours, team your team's (team admins); level server only turns own AI on or off for everyone (ownProviders, administrators). A choice names me:<name>, team:<name>, or builtin for this server's model (set in Admin → AI control). Keys are stored encrypted and never returned. Returns the settings as ai.get does. A token needs ai:admin as well for level team or server. Own AI is optional, on Slatebox Cloud and self-hosted alike. On Slatebox Cloud requests it serves spend no Slatebox credits, and an address must be public https.

message.description: A concise, natural response describing exactly what will change. Do not claim an operation that is absent from operations.

operations.description: The operations, applied in order. Each operation's kind decides which fields it may carry; any other field is refused. Fields by kind: add_nodes: count, shape, preset, text, ids, x, y, width, height, placement, style, media; update_nodes: target, changes; delete_nodes: target; duplicate_nodes: target, offset, ids; connect_nodes: from, to, ids, style; disconnect_nodes: from, to, connectionIds; update_connections: from, to, connectionIds, changes; arrange_nodes: target, layout, gap; update_slate: changes. add_nodes requires count (1 to 20): one add_nodes may add several notes (count 3, ids ["a","b","c"]) or one (count 1, ids ["a"]). connect_nodes names its new connectors with ids (one per pair); connectionIds is only for disconnect_nodes and update_connections. Examples: {"kind":"add_nodes","count":1,"ids":["title"],"shape":"rectangle","text":"Title","x":0,"y":0,"width":240,"height":80}; {"kind":"add_nodes","count":2,"ids":["a","b"],"shape":"rectangle","text":"Step","placement":{"relativeTo":"title","direction":"below","arrangement":"row"}}; {"kind":"connect_nodes","from":{"ids":["title"]},"to":{"ids":["a"]},"ids":["title-a"]}; {"kind":"update_nodes","target":{"ids":["a"]},"changes":{"text":"First step"}}.

items.description: Fields by kind (any other field is refused). add_nodes: count, shape, preset, text, ids, x, y, width, height, placement, style, media; update_nodes: target, changes; delete_nodes: target; duplicate_nodes: target, offset, ids; connect_nodes: from, to, ids, style; disconnect_nodes: from, to, connectionIds; update_connections: from, to, connectionIds, changes; arrange_nodes: target, layout, gap; update_slate: changes. add_nodes requires count.

kind.description: Which operation this is; it decides the fields the operation may carry.

count.description: add_nodes only, and required there: how many notes it adds, 1 to 20. With ids, count is normally ids.length (never fewer). Other kinds take no count.

oneOf.description: A custom shape: one SVG path (several closed parts and holes allowed, no markup), as shapes.generate or shapes.list return it.

d.description: Path data: commands and plain numbers only.

fillRule.description: evenodd when the shape has holes.

ref.description: The shape library entry it came from.

preset.description: add_nodes: text (no fill or border) or sticky (a sticky note), as the note toolbar makes them. Gives the shape when none is given.

ids.description: add_nodes and duplicate_nodes: new note ids (1 to 64 letters, digits, _ or -), which later operations in the plan may name. connect_nodes: ids for the new connectors, one per pair. An id already in use is refused.

connectionIds.description: disconnect_nodes and update_connections only: ids of connectors already on the slate. connect_nodes names its new connectors with ids, never connectionIds.

offset.description: duplicate_nodes: how far the copies sit from the notes copied; 20, 20 when left out.

placement.description: add_nodes: where to put the notes. With x and y, only arrangement and gap apply. connect: true with relativeTo makes notes that copy that note's look and are joined to it, 75 from its edge, as the canvas's connection handles do.

media.description: add_nodes, count 1, no shape, preset or text: a media note, a video from YouTube, Vimeo or Loom drawn as its poster with a play button; it plays where it sits when someone presses play, never on its own. Hosts add videos through their own add-media action, which fetches the title and stores the poster.

poster.description: The poster picture: an https address, or a path on this app (/...).

style.description: add_nodes: note keys for the new notes. connect_nodes: connector keys for the new connectors.

target.description: Name notes one way: ids, text (the whole text, ignoring case and extra spaces; match: "contains" to search), within a rectangle, groupId, or all: true. A text selector matching several notes also needs all: true.

from.description: Name notes one way: ids, text (the whole text, ignoring case and extra spaces; match: "contains" to search), within a rectangle, groupId, or all: true. A text selector matching several notes also needs all: true.

to.description: Name notes one way: ids, text (the whole text, ignoring case and extra spaces; match: "contains" to search), within a rectangle, groupId, or all: true. layout.description: arrange_nodes: row, column, grid, circle; align-* and distribute-* as the canvas aligns by what you see; tidy moves notes apart until none overlaps; tree lays connected notes out in layers under their root.

field.description: The field, by id or name.

carry.description: The cards under it that come along.

gutter.description: The gap between cells, inches in sixteenths.

oneOf.description: Grid sheet: add a tile: a stamp to the tray (each drop makes a copy), or a tile on a page at a row and column (1-based). Left without a page, the first free cell of page 1, else the tray. Boards: grid.

type.description: The kind of tile: heading, text, image, question, answer-lines, word-bank, diagram, qr, panel, speech, term, sticker.

label.description: What the tile is called in the tray and in chat (“Adding fractions”). It prints only on a tile with no words of its own. Left out, its kind: “Heading”.

body.description: Its words, which are all a page prints of it: a heading’s title, a text block’s text, a question’s question, a term and its meaning on two lines, how many answer lines. Line breaks are kept.

image.description: A picture it shows (src and alt). Left out, an image tile is an empty frame that prints its words.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for an empty frame.

link.description: A QR code’s web address (http or https).

stamp.description: True for a stamp that stays in the tray.

oneOf.description: Grid sheet: put a tile in a cell of a page (row and column from 1), spanning rows by columns. A stamp is copied there and stays in the tray. Boards: grid.

card.description: The tile, or a stamp in the tray.

page.description: The page, or the tray to take it off the page.

override.description: True to place it anyway when a limit or the sheet’s tiles refuse it, once the person agreed. Never past a page’s edge or over another tile.

oneOf.description: Grid sheet: change what a tile holds: its words, word bank, picture (null takes it away), QR address (null takes it away) or kind. Boards: grid.

shuffle.description: True to shuffle the copied terms among their cells.

edits.description: Applied in order, all or none, by the rules a person meets on the canvas. Name a card or lane by its id ({id}) or by what people call it ("the Proposal stage"). workshop.edits lists the edits this board takes.

boardId.description: The board (slates.get boards[].id; main is the first). Required when the slate holds several boards.

WorkshopEditsPlan.description: Edit a workshop the way people do: add, move, rename and remove cards and lanes. Additions and changes save at once; an edit that removes a card, a lane, a dependency or an outcome waits for the person to agree. A refusal answers 409 edit_refused with the sentence a person sees (details.reason), details.editIndex and the board as it stands; nothing is saved.

receiptId.description: The receiptId a saved workshop edit of yours answered with.

boardId.description: The board (slates.get boards[].id; main is the first). Required when the slate holds several boards.

WorkshopUndoPlan.description: Put the workshop back as it was before one of your saved edits, only while nothing has changed since (otherwise 409 slate_changed with the board as it stands).

component.description: The library entry to add (components.list ids). Or name a shared library item with library instead.

itemId.description: A smart component from library.list (kind component), or one of your own.

library.description: A smart component from the shared library (in place of component).

topic.description: What it is about: names the board ("Retro: Q3 launch").

AddComponentPlan.description: Add a library component (components.list) to this slate, the way the chat's Add does: its board goes beside the slate's notes and boards, covering none, and open pages draw it at once. The answer names its boardId (main for a slate's first board). A slate holds up to 8 boards; past that, 409 component_opens_new_slate. Preview to see the board and where it goes; saving requires an Idempotency-Key.

laneIds.description: All lane or station IDs exactly once, in presentation order. Board positions and routes stay intact.

boardId.description: The board (slates.get boards[].id; main is the first). Required when the slate holds several boards.

toId.description: Another card of the workshop, or an ordinary note of the slate by its note ID. To disconnect, it can also be the id of one of the card's lines (workshop.lines[].id): the only way to name a line whose end is free on the canvas (toPoint).

boardId.description: The board (slates.get boards[].id; main is the first). Required when the slate holds several boards.

items.description: Lane workshops: draw a line from a card to another card or to a note (connect), or take away every line between them, or one of the card's lines by its id (disconnect). The lines stay with the card wherever it moves, on or off the lanes.

boardId.description: The board (slates.get boards[].id; main is the first). Required when the slate holds several boards.

launch.description: Launch plans: launch day, and the day the last task ends (name: what the plan calls its line, such as go-live).

clock.description: Launch and hiring plans with dates: the plan's first day (YYYY-MM-DD); every day is an offset from it.

runway.description: Months of runway with these hires.

hiring.description: Hiring plans: cash, monthly burn without new hires, role bands (cost per band, never per person), the funding round, and runway.

forecast.description: Pipelines: the target, and the forecast (Σ amount × chance, plus won).

budget.description: Budgets: the total the teams split, and the step money moves in.

experience.description: The starter experience this board is, or null.

fixed.description: What this board keeps as it came, in the sentence it answers a change with; null where it may change.

presentationOrder.description: All lane or station IDs exactly once, in presentation order. Board positions and routes stay intact.

caption.description: The line under the lane on the canvas: "2 of 3", "4 / 8 points", "$300 · ...".

load.description: Release plans: points planned in this release.

probability.description: Pipelines: the chance a deal in this open stage is won, 0 to 1.

role.description: Pipelines: the stage that holds won or lost deals.

allocation.description: Budgets: what this team is given.

committed.description: Budgets: what this team’s line items add up to.

floor.description: Budgets: the least this team may be given.

cap.description: Budgets: the most this team may be given.

dependsOn.description: Release plans and launch plans: the cards it waits on.

duration.description: Launch plans: the days the task takes.

lag.description: Launch plans: the days it waits after what it waits on.

start.description: Launch plans: the day it starts (derived).

end.description: Launch plans: the day it ends (derived).

slack.description: Launch plans: the days it can slip without moving the finish.

critical.description: Launch plans: on the critical path.

from.description: Dated plans: the calendar day it starts (an offset from clock.origin).

to.description: Dated plans: the calendar day after its last day; a hire's first day.

band.description: Hiring plans: the hire's role band.

amount.description: Pipelines and budgets: the deal’s or line item’s amount.

lines.description: The lines joined to its cards: fromId and toId are card IDs, or note IDs of the slate. A line whose end is free on the canvas has toPoint (canvas coordinates) in place of toId.

scenes.description: One per lane or step, in presentation order, as Present steps through them.

livePresentation.description: The presentation someone is leading now, or null: step is the viewpoint everyone is on (-1 is the whole slate).

operations.description: The operation kinds the operations route takes on this board.

edits.description: The edits workshop_edits takes on this board.

can.description: What this board takes, in plain words, each with a phrase that does it: what a person sees under "What else can this board do?" with the board in focus. Make the change itself with workshop_edits.

revision.description: The slate's save count. Send it as expectedRevision with an edit; a workshop or map edit uses workshop.revision.

url.description: The address you open the slate at.

embed.description: The published picture of this board and its embed code, or null when none is published.

linkRole.description: The owner only: the role the share link gives, or null.

brief.description: The brief the slate was created from.

nodeCount.description: Notes the selection matches, on every page.

suggestions.description: include=suggestions: what agents suggested here (each waiting item is a ghost people keep or discard; your own canvas saves land here too) and each agent's recent actions, with the ids decide_suggestions takes.

items.description: Every key a write sets, read back as the engine loads it, unless fields chose some.

shape.description: A shape registered with the engine (custom shapes read back as custom:<name>).

animation.description: An entrance or looping animation, or null for none.

link.description: A web address the note opens (http or https), or null to remove it.

effect.description: A note effect such as dropShadow or postItNote, or null for none.

groupId.description: Notes sharing a groupId select and move as one group; null takes the note out of its group.

templateCategory.description: Only when asked to make a note a template's category heading: names the bucket the template's AI conversation files notes under, and presentations skip the note. Not for grouping or labelling notes by theme (use groupId or text). null makes it an ordinary note.

hiddenControls.description: Controls left off this note's style bar: color (fill and border), text (text colour, size, alignment, font), shape, picture, effects, ask. The list replaces the note's whole list, so to hide one more, send the ones already hidden (the summary lists them) plus it. An empty list shows them all. Chat and exec can still change the note.

locked.description: A locked note cannot be moved, changed or deleted until it is unlocked.

connections.description: The connectors that start at a note on this page.

labelPosition.description: Where the label sits along the line, from near its start (0.05) to near its end (0.95); the middle (0.5) when unset.

ends.description: Both ends that are on notes: follow (each end takes the shortest way round its note as things move) or pinned (each end stays at the spot on its note's edge that faces the line's other end, where a following end sits).

fromEnd.description: The starting end: follow, pinned (at the spot on the note's edge facing the line's other end), or pinned to the middle of the note's top, right, bottom or left side.

toEnd.description: The far end: follow, pinned (at the spot on the note's edge facing the line's other end), or pinned to the middle of the note's top, right, bottom or left side. Not for a free end.

toNote.description: Reconnect the far end to this note (its id). A free end is attached to it. The connector keeps its id.

fromNote.description: Reconnect the starting end to this note (its id); the connector then belongs to that note and keeps its id.

toPoint.description: Leave the far end free at this point on the canvas (a saved point that stays put). Detaches it from its note if it is on one; moves it if it is already free.

fromPoint.description: Leave the starting end free at this point. The connector then belongs to the note at its far end, its arrows kept as drawn. A connector keeps at least one end on a note.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; null on the last.

available.description: Whether you may use this slate’s conversation.

starters.description: Up to three messages known to work here; select is the part to type over.

boards.description: Every board on the slate, first (main) first: {id, title, kind, origin, revision} and the same read as workshop. Name one by its id (boardId) in a workshop operation; a slate of several boards requires it.

document.description: include=full: the slate as the engine loads it {options, nodes, shareId}.

details.description: What the caller needs to choose again. move_refused: cardId, laneId, legalLaneIds, revision and the current workshop. slate_changed on a workshop: revision and workshop. invalid_operation_plan on a workshop: supported, the operation kinds this board accepts. ambiguous_selector: candidates. id_taken: ids. connector_limit: limit.
